subject: Model selection & stability plan — Polaris Analytics follow-up
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Liu <jennifer.liu@polarisanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap: model recommendations and next steps

Hi Jennifer —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have a concrete plan for your POC. High-level notes from the call: Polaris wants high factual accuracy on product attribute extraction, low hallucination risk for sensitive finance copy, and consistent token costs for budget planning.

Recommended starting models for evaluation (based on your prompt examples):
- redwood-stable-2025-12: best-known stability profile and lower token overhead
- redwood-alpha-1@v2026-01-12: stronger edge-case reasoning on our internal benchmarks but slightly higher variance on hallucination tests
- llama3-8b-q4f: cost-efficient option to validate throughput targets for the live pipeline

What I attached: a first-pass prompt set keyed to your sample transcripts (polaris_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) and a short benchmark summary showing our baseline metrics using your prompts (benchmark_summary_20260218.pdf).

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) You OK with us running the three-model eval against your prompt set in a dedicated test namespace? We can run within 48 hours.
2) If we see quality regressions after comparing versions, we propose a two-tier safeguard: canary traffic + pinning to a stable revision for production routes. I outline details below and happy to adjust based on procurement/security needs.

Pin/rollback options we typically use:
- Pin production route to a specific model bundle like redwood-alpha-1@v2026-01-12 or fall back to redwood-stable-2025-12 if regressions appear. Pinning is reversible and we can automate a rollback if regression thresholds are exceeded.
- Canary 5-10% traffic with continuous regression scoring on your prompt set; if pass, expand to 100% over a 24-48 hour window.

Please confirm 1) permission to run the evals 2) whether procurement should be looped now or after we surface results. I can also include a short SOW for approval if helpful.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: polaris_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, benchmark_summary_20260218.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: model recommendations and next steps

Ava — quick internal notes before we run anything. I ran a narrow diff overnight comparing redwood-alpha-1@v2026-01-12 against redwood-stable-2025-12 on a subset of Jennifers prompts plus additional finance-adjacent edge cases. High level: alpha-1 improves recall on attribute extraction (~6-8% absolute) but we saw an uptick in hallucination score on three prompts tied to ambiguous numeric context. I attached the internal diff (internal_diff_report_20260219.csv).

Recommendations:
- Run the external eval exactly as proposed but enable canary mode in the test namespace first and set regression alert thresholds: hallucination delta > 3% or attribute recall drop > 2% triggers immediate rollback to stable.
- For Polaris production we should pre-authorize a pin window: pin to redwood-alpha-1@v2026-01-12 for 72 hours while monitoring; if alerts fire, automatic rollback to redwood-stable-2025-12 and notify customer + CS. This avoids having to negotiate in the middle of an incident.
- Also propose we add two quick golden prompts from Polaris that are business-critical and fail the model if they change; these become the watchdog set for the canary.

Operational notes: pinning is straightforward for Hosted API routes and for Dedicated we can pin on the deployment config. For Private installs we can provide the model bundle and rollback instructions in the SOW.

Let me know and I will prepare the canary job and the regression alerts. If Ava wants, I can present the internal diff to Jennifer in plain English.

Karthik
Senior ML Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: internal_diff_report_20260219.csv
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: model recommendations and next steps

Hi Jennifer —

Thanks for confirming the scope on the call. Based on internal analysis Karthik shared, here is the operational plan we propose to minimize risk while evaluating the higher-performing variant:

Plan (48-72 hour turn):
1) We will run the three-model evaluation against polaris_prompt_set_v1.jsonl in a dedicated test namespace. Canary mode only: 5% synthetic traffic or your test load.
2) We will instrument continuous regression checks that evaluate the two critical metrics you care about (attribute recall, hallucination rate). Thresholds: hallucination delta > 3% OR recall drop > 2% will trigger an automatic rollback.
3) If alpha-1 passes canary for 24 hours, we will propose pinning production route to redwood-alpha-1@v2026-01-12 for an initial 72-hour observation window. Pin will be reversible.
4) If regression triggers during the pinned window we will auto-failover to redwood-stable-2025-12 and open a Pareto triage ticket to resolve root cause.

To proceed we need:
- Your written go-ahead to run the evals in the test namespace (reply OK to this email), and
- A short list of 2 business-critical golden prompts you want us to treat as blockers if they regress.

Links and attachments:
- Benchmark & prompt set (attached)
- Internal plan and canary configuration (internal doc in Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-polaris-eval
- HubSpot deal page: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

If procurement needs to be looped to approve a pinned window or SOW, we can wait for that approval before any production pin. For the eval we do not need procurement signoff.

ETA: we can kick the eval within 48 hours of your OK and have initial results in ~24 hours after run completion.

Thanks,
Ava
